display.title: Episode 5: Asarah B'Teves and the Song of Ani Maamin
display.summary_short: On Asarah B'Teves, Uncle Yossi explains why we remember the siege of Yerushalayim and how Moshiach will turn the sad days into Yomim Tovim; a young club member sings Ani Maamin.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on the Tenth of Teves 5742. Uncle Yossi thanks the children who wrote in to join Tzivos Hashem and to get a letter in the children's Sefer Torah, and gives the phone number and address. Returning to the Hebrew calendar, he explains that today, Asarah B'Teves, is a sad day: Shlomo HaMelech taught there is a time for everything, even a time to be sad, so that we learn from the past and improve ourselves. On this day Nevuchadnetzar's armies surrounded Yerushalayim, starving the city; the walls were breached on the 17th of Tammuz and the Beis HaMikdash destroyed on Tisha B'Av. As long as we learn Torah and keep mitzvos, Hashem, who "neither slumbers nor sleeps", protects us, and Moshiach will soon turn these days into days of joy. After the Shema, a young Tzivos Hashem member sings Ani Maamin and tells what he loves about the club. The show ends with the new number for Dial-a-Jewish-Story.
display.lesson: We remember sad days in order to improve ourselves; with Torah and mitzvos Hashem protects us, and Moshiach will turn these days into Yomim Tovim.
